clue.text: It is obvious there's one in the case

indicators.note: the word in tells us the single letter goes inside the word meaning obvious

parts.note: patent means plain or evident
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A detective declares a point plain, with one suspect left in the investigation.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'case' sounds like a detective's investigation, but here it is a doctor's case.
explanation.definitionFit: A doctor refers to a person under treatment as a case.

clue.text: Complete the course then faint

explanation.surface: A runner finishes the race and then collapses.
explanation.definitionFit: Cadets graduating from military college are said to do this, and it is also an idiom for losing consciousness.

clue.text: Considered studying telepathy

parts.note: considered means thought, as in 'I thought it over'
reading a subject means studying it, as at a British university

explanation.surface: Someone has thought about taking up the study of mind-to-mind communication.
explanation.definitionFit: Telepathy is the supposed ability to perceive another person's mind directly.

clue.text: Painter from Gettysburg

indicators.note: from says the letters are taken out of the town name that follows

explanation.surface: An artist from the Pennsylvania battlefield town.
explanation.walkthrough: William Etty was a nineteenth-century English painter of nudes.
explanation.definitionFit: William Etty was an English artist known for figure paintings.

clue.text: Wart may come a cropper along the track

indicators.note: to come a cropper is British slang for falling badly, so these letters tumble into a new order

explanation.surface: A wart may trip someone up along the path.
explanation.walkthrough: To 'come a cropper' is British slang for having a heavy fall.
explanation.definitionFit: A tramway is the rail track along which trams run.

clue.text: Are such prospects indicative of the future being in the pink?

definitions.text: Are such prospects indicative of the future being in the pink?

parts.words: Are such prospects indicative of the future being in the pink?
parts.note: prospects that look hopeful are described by the same colour word as being 'in the pink', meaning healthy

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether hopeful prospects mean good health ahead.
explanation.definitionFit: Hopeful prospects are pink-tinged in idiom, and being in the pink means looking healthy and flushed.

clue.text: But Oder meandered past the temporary earthwork

indicators.note: a river that meandered wandered about, so its letters wander into a new order

explanation.surface: The Oder river wound past a soldiers' earth fortification.
explanation.walkthrough: The Oder is a river on the German-Polish border, which suits 'meandered'.
explanation.definitionFit: A redoubt is a small field fortification, often built of banked soil.

clue.text: Heavenly-sounding island

indicators.note: sounding means the word for heavenly is said aloud and matched to a place name

parts.note: the heavens are the sky

explanation.surface: An island whose name suggests the heavens.
explanation.walkthrough: Skye is a large island off the west coast of Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: Skye is one of the Inner Hebrides, an island group off Scotland.

clue.text: Craftsman, a revolutionary leader turned saint

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its opening letter
turned says the letters of the holy person's title are rearranged

explanation.surface: A craftsman was once a revolutionary chief who became a holy figure.
explanation.definitionFit: An artisan is a skilled manual worker, a synonym for a craftsman.

clue.text: Pointers give a tingling sensation

explanation.surface: Indicators produce a prickly feeling.
explanation.definitionFit: Pins and needles are sharp pointed items, and the phrase also names the prickling felt when circulation returns to a limb.

clue.text: Handicapped worker in the pool?

parts.note: handicapped suggests short-handed, and the pool is the office typing pool, not a swimming bath

explanation.surface: A disabled employee working at the swimming baths.
explanation.definitionFit: Such a secretary takes dictation in abbreviated script and once worked in an office typing pool.

clue.text: Girl coming out of gaol

indicators.note: coming out of the prison word suggests its letters escape into a new order

explanation.surface: A girl being released from prison.
explanation.walkthrough: Gaol is the British spelling of jail.
explanation.definitionFit: Olga is a female first name of Russian origin.

clue.text: Authorised to lose its head-how unpleasant

indicators.note: losing its head means the opening letter of the synonym for authorised is dropped

parts.note: authorised means lawful, permitted by law

explanation.surface: Someone is dismayed that an official was beheaded.
explanation.definitionFit: An exclamation of distaste: something dreadful is very unpleasant.

clue.text: Double existence of an Egyptian goddess

indicators.note: double says the short word for existence appears twice

parts.note: is expresses existence, as in 'there is'

explanation.surface: A goddess of ancient Egypt leads two lives.
explanation.definitionFit: Isis was the mother goddess of ancient Egyptian religion, wife of Osiris.

clue.text: It is obvious there's one in the plot

indicators.note: in tells us the single letter is placed inside the word for plot

parts.note: a plot is a plan or scheme
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A conspirator says one member of the conspiracy is plain to see.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plot' looks like a story or a patch of land; it is a scheme.
explanation.definitionFit: Something plain is clear and evident.

clue.text: Go round the edge of a garment

explanation.surface: A tailor trims around the border of a piece of clothing.
explanation.definitionFit: To skirt is to pass along the border of something, and a skirt is clothing hanging from the waist.

clue.text: To agree entirely

parts.note: two figures that tally correspond or agree

explanation.surface: Someone agrees wholeheartedly.
explanation.definitionFit: Totally means completely or wholly.

clue.text: Received or deceived

explanation.surface: Someone was welcomed in and then fooled.
explanation.definitionFit: A guest is accepted into the house, and a dupe is fooled; the phrasal verb covers both.

clue.text: Making little noise crying

parts.note: wee is Scottish for small
a ping is a short ringing noise

explanation.surface: A child cries only quietly.
explanation.definitionFit: Weeping means shedding tears.

clue.text: Jaguar strike not official

explanation.surface: Workers at the car maker walk out without union approval.
explanation.walkthrough: Jaguar is also a British car maker, which shapes the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: The jaguar is a big untamed feline, and an unofficial walkout is called this kind of strike.

clue.text: One is going to say this

definitions.text: One is going to say this

parts.words: One is going to say this
parts.note: read 'one is going' as someone departing, and the clue asks what such a person says on leaving

explanation.surface: Someone is about to make a remark.
explanation.definitionFit: A parting word said when leaving, like farewell.

clue.text: Put out of order, called in the banker

indicators.note: in says the word for called sits inside the river

parts.note: a banker is crossword slang for a river, something with banks; the Dee is a British river
rang means phoned or called

explanation.surface: Someone telephoned the bank about a faulty account.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Banker' means a river (it has banks); the Dee flows through Wales, England and also Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: To derange is to throw into disorder.

clue.text: Hound wrong coming up at a gentle pace

parts.note: a hound is a dog

indicators.note: in a down entry coming up means the word for wrong is read from bottom to top

parts.note: a tort is a civil wrong in law

explanation.surface: A dog misbehaving approaches at a leisurely speed.
explanation.definitionFit: A dogtrot is an easy, unhurried running gait.

clue.text: Muffled peals, e'd passed away

indicators.note: muffled bells sound blurred, so the letters are blurred into a new order

explanation.surface: Muffled church bells rang as someone died.
explanation.definitionFit: Time that has gone by has passed away.

clue.text: Daily in turmoil I leave her

indicators.note: turmoil throws the remaining letters into a new order
leave says the single letter named must go from the word daily

explanation.surface: A cleaner quits a chaotic household.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leave' drops I from DAILY to give DALY, which 'in turmoil' rearranges. A daily is British for a cleaning woman.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman may be referred to as her in polite speech.

clue.text: Can go wrong at the dance

indicators.note: going wrong suggests the letters are muddled up

explanation.surface: Things may go awry at a dance party.
explanation.definitionFit: The conga is a Latin American line dance.

clue.text: A five are returning for her

parts.note: V is the Roman numeral for five

indicators.note: returning means the following word is read backwards

explanation.surface: Five people are coming back for a woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Vera is a female first name.

clue.text: Article in bed might have come out of a necklace

definitions.text: might have come out of a necklace

indicators.note: in places the article inside the word for bed

parts.note: a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A bead found in bed fell from a necklace.
explanation.definitionFit: A bead is a small pierced ball strung on a necklace.

clue.text: Nothing is in order in the orchestra

indicators.note: is in says the round letter goes inside the honour

parts.note: the OBE is the Order of the British Empire
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Nothing is in order among the musicians.
explanation.definitionFit: The oboe is a woodwind instrument found in an orchestra.

clue.text: Flowers in a cathedral tower?

explanation.surface: Blossoms adorn a church spire.
explanation.definitionFit: These are campanula plants with bell-shaped blooms, and the bells hung in Kent's great cathedral.

clue.text: Tool which, we hear, does calculations

indicators.note: we hear says the word for doing sums is said aloud

parts.note: one who adds does calculations

explanation.surface: A gadget that seems to do arithmetic.
explanation.definitionFit: An adze is a woodworking cutting implement with an arched blade.

clue.text: Locked?

parts.note: the clue's word suggests fastened with a key, but read it as having locks of hair

explanation.surface: Is something secured shut?
explanation.definitionFit: Having tresses means having long locks of hair.
